label: copy-phase input d echoed back early in the copy (recall_idx 2-4), not the final output
explanation: Token-specific feature for the letter d being fed back as input during the copy phase. It fires only when the input is d (essentially 100% of activation mass) and only in the copy phase (t > L), i.e. when d is an echoed original token, never on d in the original phase or at the delimiter. It is restricted to early-middle copy positions: recall_idx 2-4 (the fed-back d is original token 1-3), and it is silent on the last step (to_go = 0) and almost silent at recall_idx 1 and >= 5. Magnitude is largest at recall_idx 2 (d was the 2nd original token, two steps after <DEL>; top examples are all of the form x d ... <DEL> x [d]) and smaller at recall_idx 3-4. Lowest-quartile activations are mostly d in later positions or short sequences. It does not depend on the output token, the previous token, or how many digits are in the sequence.

issues: Small caveat: recall_idx 4 is the weak edge. Precision there is 0.77, against 1.0 at recall_idx 2 and 3. At L=6 (recall_idx 4 with to_go=1) precision falls to 0.54. Excluding that case shifts precision and recall but lowers test F1 slightly (0.947 vs 0.952), so it does not improve the predicate.
The leftover false positives at recall_idx 4 for L>=7 (about 15%) show no visible token or history pattern in misses. They look like near-threshold noise; mass_recall is 0.997.

The missed activations (1324 on test, 0.3% of mass) are tiny activations (0.00-0.05 relative) on d at recall_idx 1 or 5. That is scattered noise, consistent with the explanation calling those positions 'almost silent'.

The factual claims check out. All activation mass is in the copy phase and none is in the original phase or at the delimiter. Input d carries 1.000 of the mass. Mass by recall_idx is 2: 0.569, 3: 0.367, 4: 0.061. to_go=0 has only 57 activations. out_tok and prev_tok are flat at about 2.2x lift each. A second d in the copy is not suppressed: precision is 0.92 for in_count>=2 vs 0.94 for in_count==1.
